text: Supports multiple DDS middleware implementations (Cyclone DDS, Fast DDS, RTI Connext) that can be selected at runtime
quote: Support for multiple DDS implementations, chosen at runtime - Currently Eclipse Cyclone DDS, eProsima Fast DDS, and RTI Connext DDS are fully supported.

text: Uses Fast DDS as the default middleware, and the RMW layer can be swapped at runtime
quote: The default middleware that ROS 2 uses is `Fast DDS`, but the middleware (RMW) can be replaced at runtime.

text: Bridge for communication between ROS 1 and ROS 2, available for topics and services but not yet for actions
quote: ROS 1 - ROS 2 communication bridge - Available for topics and services, not yet available for actions.

text: Quality of Service policies let you tune node communication, including for non-ideal networks
quote: ROS 2 offers a rich variety of Quality of Service (QoS) policies that allow you to tune communication between nodes.

text: QoS settings can make communication as reliable as TCP, as best-effort as UDP, or anything in between
quote: With the right set of Quality of Service policies, ROS 2 can be as reliable as TCP or as best-effort as UDP, with many, many possible states in between.

text: Predefined QoS profiles for common use cases such as sensor data
quote: ROS 2 provides a set of predefined QoS profiles for common use cases (e.g. sensor data).

text: Transient-local durability gives latching-publisher behavior
quote: The "durability" policy "transient local", combined with any depth, provides functionality similar to that of "latching" publishers.

text: Node components can be composed at compile, link, load, or run time (C++ only)
quote: Composition of node components at compile, link, load, or run time - Currently only in C++.

text: Supports nodes with managed lifecycles (C++ only)

text: Launch system for coordinating multiple nodes
quote: Launch system for coordinating multiple nodes

text: Client libraries in multiple programming languages, such as Python and C++
quote: Client libraries come in a variety of programming languages so that users may write ROS 2 code in the language that is best-suited for their application.

text: Nodes written with different client libraries can exchange messages through shared code generators
quote: Nodes written using different client libraries are able to share messages with each other because all client libraries implement code generators

text: Official ros2 command-line tool with sub-commands for working with nodes, topics, services, and more
quote: The main entry point for the tools is the command ros2, which itself has various sub-commands for introspecting and working with nodes, topics, services, and more.

text: Command-line introspection tools built on an extensible framework

text: Publish and echo messages on a topic from the command line

text: Publish/subscribe over topics for continuous data streams such as sensor data
quote: The topic interface is meant for continuous data streams, for example, streaming sensor data or the status of your robot.

text: Services for synchronous request/response interactions
quote: The service interface is meant for synchronous request/response interactions, for example, when you want to send a query requesting the configuration of a specific robot.

text: Actions for long-running tasks, with goals, feedback, cancellation, and results
quote: Actions allow clients to send goals, receive feedback during the execution, cancel if needed, and return a result if available

text: Built-in topic statistics that measure message behavior at the subscription
quote: Topic statistics are built-in measurements that help you understand how messages behave when a subscription receives them.

text: Built-in security encrypts data in transit and authenticates participants across the ROS graph
quote: Built-in ROS 2 security features enable control over communications throughout the ROS graph. This not only allows for encrypting data in transit between ROS domain participants, but also enables authentication of participants sending data

text: Security enclaves each encapsulate a single policy for protecting ROS communications
quote: A security enclave encapsulates a single policy for protecting ROS communications.

text: sros2 package provides tools for running ROS 2 on top of DDS-Security
quote: The `sros2` package provides the tools and instructions to use ROS 2 on top of DDS-Security.

text: Create a security keystore with sros2 utilities to enable security for all participants
quote: Use the sros2 utilities to create the keystore. Files in the keystore will be used to enable security for all the participants in the ROS 2 graph.

text: Record subscribed topic data to a bag while processing it at the same time

text: Save non-topic data, such as synthetic training data, to bags
